title: Anaphylaxis
summary: Sudden airway/breathing/circulation compromise with likely allergen exposure — give IM adrenaline without delay.

sources.label: Resuscitation Council UK — Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis

blocks.title: Diagnose anaphylaxis when
blocks.body: Sudden onset and rapid progression of Airway and/or Breathing and/or Circulation problems, usually with skin/mucosal changes (flushing, urticaria, angioedema). Skin changes alone are NOT anaphylaxis.

items: Call for help early — resuscitation team if A/B/C compromise
Remove the trigger if possible (stop drug infusion, remove stinger)
Lie patient flat (legs raised if hypotensive); sitting up may help isolated breathing difficulty. Do NOT stand the patient up
Give IM adrenaline (see algorithm) — do not delay for IV access or monitoring
High-flow oxygen; attach monitoring (SpO₂, ECG, BP) as soon as available

steps.detail: Adrenaline 500 micrograms IM (0.5 mL of 1 mg/mL / 1:1000) into anterolateral mid-thigh — verify against local policy.
If no improvement in A/B/C problems, repeat IM adrenaline 500 micrograms. Repeat every 5 min as needed.
steps.branch: Improving → continue monitoring; period of observation (biphasic reactions occur)

steps.detail: IV crystalloid bolus 500–1000 mL for shock/poor response; reassess and repeat as needed — verify against local policy.

No improvement despite 2 appropriate doses of IM adrenaline → follow refractory algorithm: get expert help, start low-dose IV adrenaline infusion (critical care/experienced clinician only), continue fluids.
steps.branch: Cardiac arrest → start CPR and follow ALS

steps.detail: Observe for biphasic reaction (length per local policy and risk). Consider non-sedating oral antihistamine and steroids for persisting skin symptoms only — they are NOT first-line treatment. Take timed serum mast cell tryptase samples. Refer to allergy services; prescribe adrenaline auto-injector and educate before discharge.

blocks.title: Common pitfalls
blocks.body: IV bolus adrenaline is hazardous outside cardiac arrest and should only ever be given by specialists via infusion. Antihistamines and steroids are not substitutes for adrenaline. Beware sudden standing/sitting up — it can precipitate cardiac arrest (empty ventricle syndrome).

blocks.title: Why IM and why the thigh?
blocks.body: IM adrenaline into the vastus lateralis achieves rapid, reliable absorption with a wide safety margin. Its α₁ effects reverse vasodilation and mucosal oedema while β effects bronchodilate and stabilise mast cells. The 5-minute reassess-and-repeat cycle exists because absorption and clinical response vary — many patients need more than one dose.
